title: A GPO with its user side disabled contributes nothing to the user scope

provenance.note: RELOCATED from disabled-block-enforced 2026-08-04 (WI-029), not newly authored. That scenario was blocked in full for this single HKCU assertion while the rest of it was computer-scope and runnable; moving the assertion here freed the other half for WP-6B and kept this claim visible instead of dropping it. The computer-side half -- that MachineVal still applies from the same GPO -- is now WP-6B-verified, so this scenario asserts only the part that needs the user scope.

operator_meaning: A GPO whose user side is disabled must contribute nothing to the user scope
The same GPO's computer side must still apply -- verified by WP-6B, restated here only as the control that makes the absence meaningful

winners.reason: user side disabled contributes nothing to the user scope
CONTROL: the computer side still applies. WP-6B observed this on a real 26200 client. If it is absent here, the GPO did not apply at all and the HKCU absence above says nothing.

derivations: A disabled side removes only that scope's contribution; the other side is unaffected. The computer-side half of this claim is WP-6B-verified; the user-side half is what this scenario exists to test.

open_questions: ANSWERED 2026-08-04: gpresult /x /scope:user OMITS the GPO from UserResults entirely rather than reporting it applied-with-no-settings. The certified run observed UserWinner and Control from the two enabled GPOs and nothing from Studio-RSOP-UserSideOff, whose user side was disabled.
